hero.title: Kolabr vs Zendesk
hero.lede: Zendesk is built to keep customers at the door: a portal, a form, a queue, a reply by email and a ticket that closes. Kolabr brings your clients into the room. They ask in the channel they already use, the person who knows the answer gives it, and the clock on every request is there for them to see.

chip.title: Fixed in nine minutes
chip.body: Raised in the channel, answered by the engineer who knew, confirmed by the client.

journey.title: One request, two journeys
journey.lede: The same Monday-morning problem, from the moment the client notices it to the moment it is fixed.

steps.text: Emails support, or fills in the web form.
A ticket is created and waits its turn.
Picks it up and reads back through the history.
Asks the engineer who knows, in a private note.
Answers the agent, not the client.
Passes the answer on to the client by email.
The ticket is solved and closed. The next question starts a new one.
Says it in the channel they are already in.
One step makes it request #2214, with an owner and a one-hour response target.
The person who knows answers in the thread.
Watches the owner, the status and the clock, and confirms the fix.
The request closes and stays in the channel’s history, beside the wiki article that stops it happening again.

keep.title: Clients, not tickets
keep.lede: What your guests keep in a channel that a queue was never built to give them.

tiles.title: One place, for years
tiles.body: Every request, decision and article for that client lives in one channel. Nothing is closed away from the conversation that produced it.

tiles.title: The clock in plain sight
tiles.body: Each request shows its owner, its status and the time left, to your guests, without anyone logging in to a portal to check.

tiles.title: People with names
tiles.body: Your guests see who is working on their request and talk to them directly, not to a shared support address.

cost.title: What response targets cost
cost.lede: In Zendesk, response targets start at Suite Professional. In Kolabr they are on Pro. Choose how many users you have.

items.title: Is Kolabr a helpdesk?
items.body: No. A helpdesk is built to process volume from people you will never meet: a portal, a queue, macros and a ticket that closes. Kolabr is built for clients you know by name and keep for years. They are in the channel with you, and each request is one part of an ongoing conversation rather than a case in a queue.

items.title: Do clients need to log into a portal?
items.body: No. They are in the channel, which is where they already talk to you. There is no separate system to learn, no password to forget and no moment where somebody gives up and sends an email instead.

items.title: Can the people who know the answer reply to clients directly?
items.body: Yes. Every user can answer in the channels they are in. In Zendesk, replying to a customer needs an agent licence; a light agent can add private notes but cannot reply.

items.title: Do we get response targets on the entry plan?
items.body: Yes. Response targets are on Kolabr Pro, and your guests can see them. In Zendesk they start at Suite Professional, $115 per agent a month on yearly terms.

items.title: Which is cheaper?
items.body: On yearly terms Kolabr Pro is $8.50 per user a month, against $55 per agent for Zendesk Suite Team and $115 for Suite Professional, the first Suite plan with response targets. For 10 people that is $85 a month, against $550 and $1,150.

items.title: What is in the Kolabr price?
items.body: Chat, requests with response targets, routing, playbooks, a wiki in every channel, video calls and scheduled events, all on Pro. Nothing is billed per agent or per resolution.

proof.title: Proof takes one week
proof.lede: Take one client off the portal. Nothing else has to change, and the rest of the queue carries on exactly as it is.

steps.text: Give that client a channel, invite everyone on their side as guests, and add any colleague of yours who could help. Nobody needs a helpdesk licence.
Requests are arriving from people who never bothered to log in, and answers are coming from colleagues who never had a helpdesk licence.
You will know what the portal was costing you in questions nobody asked. That is the only test this page is asking you to run.

cta.title: Take one client off the portal.
cta.body: Free for one channel, no card. Seven days on Pro or Business when you want the rest. Keep the owners, categories and clocks; lose the front door.
